html:
A Turkish novelist from Istanbul who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2006, the first Turk to do so. He is Turkey's best selling writer.

He grew up in a well-off, Westernised family, studied architecture and journalism, and gave his life to writing. Most of his novels are set in Istanbul and deal with a question that runs through modern Turkey: how East and West, old and new, religious and secular, live together.

His best known books include:

  • The White Castle (1985) and The Black Book (1990);
  • My Name Is Red (1998), a murder mystery among miniature painters of the Ottoman court in 1591;
  • Snow (2002), about political Islam and secularism in a snowbound eastern town;
  • Istanbul: Memories and the City (2003), a memoir of the city's melancholy;
  • The Museum of Innocence (2008). He also opened a real museum of the same name in Istanbul.

In 2005 he told a Swiss paper that a million Armenians and thirty thousand Kurds had been killed in Turkey and no one dared talk about it. He was charged with insulting Turkishness, a case that drew world protest, and the charges were dropped. See also the Armenian genocide.
